sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source on Sources for attribution limits.

strict.criterion: Three-dimensional multilayer circuit architectures become common across general-purpose computing logic as well as memory.
strict.rationale: Samsung began mass-producing 3D V-NAND flash memory in 2013, bringing genuine multilayer active circuitry into mainstream storage. However, general-purpose CPUs and GPUs still rely on planar CMOS logic (with 2.5D/3D chiplet stacking rather than monolithic 3D transistor-lattice circuits), leaving the strict computing-circuit claim partial.
changedConditions: Distinguishes 3D flash memory from general-purpose 3D logic processors

reference.criterion: Multilayer active circuitry moves from experiments into ordinary semiconductor products.
reference.rationale: Early stacked/specialized devices made the direction real, but a broad transition to genuinely three-dimensional circuitry was only partial in 2009. Samsung’s mass-produced 3D V-NAND from 2013 establishes commercial multilayer circuits. The word “common” need not mean every processor has become 3D.

broader.criterion: Multilayer 3D active semiconductor circuits become a mainstream commercial product category, including 3D flash memory.
broader.rationale: Specialized die-stacking existed before 2009, but independent evidence of truly common 3D integrated circuits arrives with Samsung's 2013 mass production of 3D V-NAND flash rather than before the 2009 deadline.
changedConditions: Counts mass-market 3D NAND memory as fulfilling 3D integrated circuits
